props.title: Oh, God! You Devil
props.initialSlug: Heaven and hell in one soul.

sections.content: Oh, God! You Devil (1984) marks George Burns' fascinating dual role as both God and Satan, capping off the quirky Oh, God! trilogy that began in 1977. While the original film co-starring John Denver tackled faith with gentle humor, this final installment goes darker, following a struggling musician who makes a Faustian bargain. Burns becomes the first actor to play both God and the Devil in the same film, predating similar dual divine/demonic castings like Peter Stormare and Tilda Swinton in Constantine (2005) or Al Pacino's Satan opposite Morgan Freeman's God in Devil's Advocate (1997).

sections.content: The 1980s saw a fascinating wave of supernatural comedies mixing faith and laughs. Oh, God! You Devil shares DNA with films like All of Me (1984) and Heaven Can Wait (1978), where metaphysical concepts get a light touch. This era's religious-themed comedies often used star power to make divine concepts accessible - think Trading Places (1983) testing fate and free will, or Ghost (1990) turning the afterlife into romantic comedy territory. SUBHEAD: The Devil in American Cinema

Burns' Satan follows a rich tradition of charismatic Devils in American film. From Walter Huston's subtle Mr. Scratch in The Devil and Daniel Webster (1941) to Jack Nicholson's devilish charm in The Witches of Eastwick (1987), Satan often appears as a smooth-talking dealmaker rather than a purely evil force. This characterization continues through Elizabeth Hurley in Bedazzled (2000) and Peter Stormare's memorable white-suited Lucifer in Constantine (2005).
